chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadda', from Muhammad ibn al-Is, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys something that is tasted, should he taste it before buying? He said, 'Yes, let him taste it, and let him not taste what he does not buy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on tasting food before buying it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of conditional sales (bay' al-taslim) by distinguishing between sampling for quality assessment and actual consumption. It establishes that the right to taste is contingent upon the finalization of the purchase, preventing unjust enrichment if the deal falls through. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring that the seller's property rights are preserved until the contract is complete.
